description.narrative: Supporting an inclusive transition to a “green” economy in the Agri-food sector and development of a “climate-smart” Uzbek Agriculture Knowledge and Innovation System (UAKIS)

condition.narrative: Consistent with the Article III of the SBAA [or the Supplemental Provisions to the Project Document], the responsibility for the safety and security of the Implementing Partner and its personnel and property, and of UNDP’s property in the Implementing Partner’s custody, rests with the Implementing Partner. comment.narrative:
Almost half of the population in Uzbekistan lives and works in rural areas and although the share of agriculture as a % of GDP has been declining steadily, it plays an important role in the socio-economic life of the country. The agricultural sector comprises 28% of GDP (2019) and employs circa 33.2% of the working population. Moreover, up to 49% of the population’s income is supplemented by agricultural activities. However, intensive farming practices have degraded much of the available arable land and depleted the water resources. Irrigation currently consumes over 90% of total water withdrawals. Despite agricultural reforms to improve irrigation efficiency, Uzbekistan faces significant challenges with desertification and water scarcity – all of which are exacerbated by climate stressors.
Uzbekistan has taken steps to include climate change considerations across national policy. One of the steps towards this was the approval of the Strategy for the transition of Uzbekistan to the green economy for the period 2019-2030 which includes climate change considerations. However, to date, a comprehensive framework for climate change adaptation is still lacking. Climate change is addressed, to some extent, in various policy documents, such as the Water Saving and Rational Water Use in Irrigated Land Tenure Strategy, the Uzbekistan Agri-food Development Strategy, National Strategy for Adaptation of Public Health Care System to Climate Change, strategies for adaptation of forestry to climate change, including the Forest Code, National Forest Programme, etc. However, they have not been developed within an overarching climate change policy framework, and still have a sectoral emphasis and are integrated with sector-specific economic development strategies.
Draft UAKIS Strategy r is adopted (Concept); Operationalization plan for CC mitigation and adaptation in the Agri-food sector not available

1.1 Assessment of policy and regulatory barriers to scaled-up climate action and “green” transition is in progress 1.2 3 knowledge products, namely Thextbook Global Climate and Water Supply and Guideline on Operational/Innovation Groups developed 1.3 31 policy makers informed about the new knowledge products 1.4 44 of professional staff and researchers trained
More detailed information: 1.1. Support and facilitate improvements in the policy and regulatory framework for effective implementation of the Agri-food Innovation Support and Brokerage Services and for scaled-up climate action in the agri-food sector ? Work has begun on conducting a baseline assessment of agricultural production in pilot Tashkent and Fergana regions to support development of agri-food strategies of these regions. ? Study on policy, regulatory and financial barriers for innovation in climate action and ‘green transition in the agri-food sector in progress, including detailed analysis of following: - Protection of intellectual property rights (for new seeds and plant varieties); - Regulation and access to energy markets (for renewable energy sources); - Establishment of public-private partnerships; - Assessment of the environmental impact of price and income support policies for agriculture; - Promoting regulatory and financial incentives for climate-smart agriculture practices and technologies.
1.2. Building institutional capacity and partnerships among UAKIS stakeholders to effectively deliver Agri-food Innovation Support and Brokerage Services ? On June 1-2, the project and other partner organizations organized the 2nd National Agricultural and Food Research Forum on the theme Uzbekistan on the road to development: transformation of agricultural and food research ? The project announced 5 biddings for procure the lab equipment to strengthen the material and technical base of research institutes, local agricultural colleges and universities that provide consulting services
1.3. Participatory planning and identification of project portfolios ? The project conduct practical trainings with research institutes in order to increase their knowledge and skills in drafting proposals for innovative projects
1.4. Establishing continuous feedback, learning and knowledge management system under UAKIS To be started next year
2.1. Establishing the Agri-food Innovation Operational Groups and soliciting innovative proposals on climate-smart agriculture and transition to “green” agri-food value chains ? The project conducts regular practical trainings with research institutes in order to increase their knowledge and skills in drafting proposals for innovative projects. After training conducted on project proposal, research institutions formulated innovation project on the base of produced template and sent to the project. Project reviews proposals and provide with comments for the improvement. This is ongoing process.
Next step is the grant application procedure that should address the following: ? After a preliminary call for proposals, an initial screening will be conducted and only those projects eligible will be further considered for funding support. ? Approved proposals will be invited to prepare detailed Innovation Group Project proposals with support from the project team. ? Innovation Group Project proposals/ plans would need to comply with national environmental safeguard policies. ? Women-led business proposals will be provided with additional assistance in meeting the criteria and building their capacity to become economically viable and sustainable. ? A Selection Committee will approve the Innovation Group Project proposals following internal validation and recommendations by the Project Team. ? The Project Team will support promotional events to inform and attract potential IG proposals.
This is a long process with high risk of delay in implementation od IG project taking into account short project cycle and seasonal nature of sub-projects. Another option, i.e., RPA modality providing endorsement of EU and the PB.
2.2. Delivery of training, capacity building and technical advice to the members and partners of the Agri-food Innovation Operational Groups ? In cooperation with Women of Agrarian Industry association, a practical seminar was organized for 162 rural women aimed at organizing proper care of cows, healthy breeding, increasing productivity and cooperative processing of produced milk in households. ? With the participation of the international expert of the project, David Kahan, a seminar-training on Organization of innovative groups for national stakeholders conducted ? A 2-day seminar training aimed at writing innovative project proposals for representatives of research institutions, AKIS, THVET and farmers conducted on the base of developed Guideline for the implementation of operational/innovation groups.
2.3. Delivering targeted financial support and investments for innovative projects with climate change mitigation and adaptation benefits ? Technical status of scientific-research institutes and experimental stations in the pilot regions in terms of their ability to support operational/innovation groups were studied. Now, the purchase of laboratory equipment for the ITI within the innovative groups is being carried out. ? The Guideline for the implementation of operational/innovation groups developed
2.4. Innovation networking and exchange program to promote uptake in other regions/areas To be started next year
